extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers, scholarly reviewers, and early-career reviewers writing reader reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing developmental peer-review reports (reader reports) for scholarly articles and books that are constructive, focused, and usable by authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize the big picture
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify three major areas that would benefit from revision rather than overwhelming with minor corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize and highlight a small number of substantive, high-impact issues so authors can focus effort. Avoid long lists of petty edits that drown the main points; group related minor issues under broader headings when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain feedback thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid vague comments like 'this was confusing' — specify why something is unclear (e.g., chronological jumps without transitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific examples from the text, point to the passage, and explain the source of confusion. Describe what the confusion prevents (e.g., disrupts argument flow, obscures method) and, where possible, suggest concrete ways to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a kind, encouraging tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Write reviews with a considerate, supportive voice; imagine the author as a respected colleague when rereading your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the report aside and reread to check tone; avoid harsh or personal phrasing. Frame critiques constructively, emphasize improvement, and avoid language that could be perceived as attacking the author's competence or motives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out what works well so the author remains open to suggestions instead of feeling entirely criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance criticism with positive feedback about strong arguments, effective evidence, clear prose, or valuable contributions. Specific praise helps authors recognize what to preserve during revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor length
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep reports a manageable length: a few pages for articles and longer for books; reports longer than about 10 pages can overwhelm and hide main points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and structured (e.g., summary, major issues, minor issues). Use headings or numbered lists to make key recommendations easy to locate. For books or extensive manuscripts, longer reports are acceptable but still prioritize clarity and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the author's vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not criticize an approach simply because you'd write differently; evaluate how successfully the author accomplishes their stated mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the work against its own goals and stated aims rather than the reviewer's personal stylistic or theoretical preferences. If you think the chosen approach limits the work, explain why in relation to the author's objectives and suggest alternatives if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit timely reviews — punctuality matters for authors' careers and publication timelines. If too busy, decline graciously and suggest alternative reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate promptly with editors if you cannot meet a deadline. Declining is preferable to a late, rushed review. When declining, offer names of qualified alternative reviewers if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace diverse forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain open to nontraditional scholarly structures and voices that serve the author's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize unconventional formats or narrative strategies if they effectively realize the author's aims. Evaluate innovation in form on how well it supports argumentation, evidence, and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit norm: avoid substituting your preferences for the author's argument
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer who substitutes their own preferences for the author's argument has stopped reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against letting personal taste dictate substantive critique. Focus on whether the work achieves its goals and contributes usefully to its field rather than reshaping it to match the reviewer's individual preferences.
